The mental pocket primitive models sensation as a discrete cognitive state with binary filling. It assumes isolation of sensory knowledge, leading to the cum alio paradox where isolated sensations cannot integrate. The paradox fails under holistic neural field coupling, where sensory inputs map to unified consciousness states. The neural field primitive asserts that retinal input remains constant while consciousness varies, implying a dynamic transformation layer. This suggests that sensation is not atomistic but emergent from field interactions. The failure mode occurs when discrete pockets cannot interface with global neural states, violating coherence principles. The resolution lies in treating sensation as a field variable rather than a point mass.
